title: Building a drumming style from Jo Jones, Chick Webb, Catlett and Sonny Greer
summary: Leeman says drummers compile ideas from others: Zutty Singleton, Chick Webb, Sid Catlett, Baby Dodds, Jo Jones's hi-hat trick and Sonny Greer's way of pushing a band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You don't copy anybody. Some people do. From what I had learned from Zutty Singleton, who Shaw made me listen to, and what little things I had learned
(K see p.5 for explanation of this)

from Chick Webb, and later on, I got to know a person called Sidney Catlett that was electrifying to me, and this all happened during the era -- and when Sidney was with Louis Armstrong's band, and you compile little things -- Baby Dodds, as we mentioned before, and you take a little bit here and a little bit there and it goes in your memory, it goes in your technique -- I don't know of anybody who is so completely original that you can say he doesn't sound like anybody who ever lived, except Prez came along with a style, but you had to listen to people to develop a style.

So without trying to copy anybody, I came as close to playing -- like things were great, like Jo Jones was something that sunk into my skin there from Jo, and I got that little trick of his from way back in Kansas City ...

Of playing behind the piano or something like -- the piano, mostly, he used to play behind. Outside of the open cymbals, but he used to play with one stick on the side of the high hat, and of course he's the greatest artist in the world -- and the other hand, and I developed a little thing out of that, which you've heard me on any of the records with the small bands that I play, and that got under my skin from Jo Jones. And I could develop this with the

great respect I had -- I couldn't possibly have liked Duke Ellington. Well, just love him, my dear, dear friend -- Sonny Greer, who was not a great cymbaler -- but what he did to that band was what I tried to do to push a band, to get underneath it.
Well, you certainly have done that down through the years.
